issues.description: Invariant 'req.prepared / needs_more_preparation are set after resolve' is silently broken.
issues.detail: The resolver previously established the post-condition that every requirement is fully prepared with prepared=True and needs_more_preparation=False. The new code deletes that block without stating who now owns the invariant. Each command must remember to call prepare_linked_requirements_more, and any future command path will be wrong by default. State the invariant explicitly in a comment or restore enforcement.

issues.description: set_dist/get_dist priority order is undocumented and may shadow a fully-prepared distribution.
issues.detail: get_dist now returns self._distribution first, before metadata_directory or local_file_path. If set_dist caches a metadata-only BaseDistribution and the requirement is later fully prepared (metadata_directory populated), callers receive the stale metadata-only dist. The invariant 'cached dist is upgraded or invalidated on full prepare' is neither stated nor enforced.

issues.description: download_info fallback is set unconditionally with no comment justifying correctness for non-PEP-658 paths.
issues.detail: When metadata_dist is non-None, download_info is overwritten with direct_url_from_link(req.link, req.source_dir) if None. For a metadata-only fetch, req.source_dir may not yet exist or may not contain a hash; direct_url_from_link's contract here deserves a literate comment explaining what download_info means in the dry-run case and why a hash-less URL is acceptable for `pip lock`.

issues.description: Three command sites duplicate the same prepare_linked_requirements_more call with no shared helper.
issues.detail: download.py, install.py, and wheel.py now each call preparer.prepare_linked_requirements_more(requirement_set.requirements.values()) at the top of their post-resolve block. This is the exact code the resolver used to own. The right data structure here is a single 'finalize_resolution' step; otherwise the next command added will forget the call. Not a correctness bug today, but a maintainability time bomb.

issues.description: No test cited proving --dry-run actually avoids the wheel download.
issues.detail: The news fragment claims dry-run no longer downloads full wheels, but the diff shows no test asserting that the network/cache is not hit for a PEP-658 metadata path. 'I have only proved it correct, not tried it' applies: add a test that fails on the old behavior and passes on the new one, otherwise the regression will return silently.

set_dist unconditionally overwrites self._distribution. If the same requirement is prepared twice (e.g., via a retry or a graph cycle in extras), a later metadata-only dist could replace a richer one. Either assert self._distribution is None on set, or document that last-writer-wins is intentional. A one-line invariant comment would suffice.

review.summary: The change moves the 'more preparation' step out of the resolver and into the install/download/wheel commands, with a new cached-distribution slot on InstallRequirement. The algorithmic intent is sound and the asymptotic win is real for dry-run and lock. However, the diff silently retires a post-condition that the resolver used to enforce (prepared=True, needs_more_preparation=False) and replaces it with an implicit contract scattered across three command files. The new set_dist/get_dist pair lacks a stated invariant about priority and freshness, which is exactly the kind of thing that will rot. Code is plausibly correct; the literate explanation and a regression test are missing. UNDER-AUDITED, NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT.
